title: I could keep the Ape only by staying tapped
era: 1994 Worlds representative matchup under current Oracle rules
matchup: U/W/G Stasis Control against red-green midrange
story: My Old Man of the Sea had been under my control since the start of the turn. I tapped it targeting an opposing Kird Ape , whose Taiga made it a 2/3. The Ape had power two, no greater than the Old Man's power two, so the ability resolved and I gained control. During my next untap step I chose not to untap the Old Man. The stolen Ape remained on my side. If I let Old Man untap or my opponent raised the Ape's power above two, the theft would end. I could not simply forget the tap condition.
review: Old Man 2/3 has continuous control while tapped and target power at most 2. Kird Ape + Taiga 2/3 qualifies. On controller next untap choose not to untap. Fictional opponent.
claim: representative reconstruction; not a historical match or quotation
